topic: NVIDIA-Certified Associate: Accelerated Data Science (NCA-ADS) exam preparation - NVIDIA's associate certification for GPU-accelerated data science with the RAPIDS ecosystem (cuDF, cuML, cuGraph, Dask), covering data manipulation, ETL and scalable pipelines, machine learning, advanced analytics, and GPU environments
exam_format: Online, remotely proctored. Approximately 50-60 multiple-choice questions with a 60-minute time limit; associate-level credential. Registration is via NVIDIA's certification portal. NVIDIA does NOT publicly publish the passing score or official per-domain percentage weightings for NCA-ADS, so the domain weights in this course are editorial estimates that reflect the emphasis of the published exam objective areas and NVIDIA's Deep Learning Institute accelerated-data-science curriculum, not NVIDIA's official figures. A professional-tier variant (NCP-ADS) also exists; this course targets the Associate (NCA-ADS). Exam pricing varies by region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current NVIDIA pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options); scenario- and tool-decision questions about GPU-accelerated data science with the RAPIDS ecosystem
audience: Data scientists, data engineers, ML practitioners, and analysts who work in Python (pandas, scikit-learn) and want to move to GPU-accelerated data science with NVIDIA RAPIDS. Candidates should be comfortable with core data-manipulation and ML concepts and basic Python. The GPU / hardware-acceleration focus (RAPIDS, GPU architecture, cloud GPU environments) pairs it with the AI-infrastructure and NVIDIA certifications in this catalog (NCA-AIIO, NCP-AIO, NCA-GENL, NCP-GENL, NCP-AAI, NCP-OUSD).
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: GPU-Accelerated Data Manipulation and Preparation
domains.notes: The core RAPIDS skill: cuDF as a GPU DataFrame and its relationship to pandas (near-drop-in API, differences, cudf.pandas accelerator). Cleaning, joining, filtering, grouping, and reshaping data on the GPU; dtypes and memory layout; handling nulls and strings; and generating synthetic data with RAPIDS. Knowing when a cuDF operation beats pandas and when to fall back. Choosing the correct GPU data-manipulation approach for a described dataset and constraint.

domains.name: ETL and Scalable GPU Pipelines
domains.notes: GPU-accelerated ETL and scaling beyond a single GPU: Dask and dask-cuDF for distributed/out-of-core processing, partitioning, and multi-GPU workflows; data caching and I/O formats (Parquet, ORC) for throughput; and selecting the right library and execution model for data at scale. Pipeline design for performance and efficiency. Choosing between single-GPU cuDF, multi-GPU Dask, or CPU pandas for a described data volume and pipeline.

domains.name: Machine Learning with cuML and Feature Engineering
domains.notes: GPU-accelerated machine learning with cuML: its scikit-learn-like API, supported algorithms (regression, classification, clustering, dimensionality reduction, nearest neighbors), and train/predict/evaluate workflow. Feature engineering on the GPU (encoding, scaling, transformations) and hyperparameter tuning at speed. Knowing when cuML accelerates a workload versus scikit-learn. Selecting the correct cuML algorithm or feature-engineering step for a described modeling task.

domains.name: Advanced and Graph Analytics
domains.notes: Beyond tabular ML: exploratory data analysis (EDA) on the GPU, time-series analysis, and anomaly detection. Graph analytics with cuGraph - building graphs from edge lists and running algorithms (PageRank, centrality, community detection, traversal) at GPU scale. Choosing the correct analytic technique or cuGraph algorithm for a described question about data relationships or patterns.

domains.name: GPU Architecture, Environments, and Performance
domains.notes: The hardware-acceleration foundation: GPU architecture basics (why data-parallel workloads accelerate), GPU vs CPU memory, and GPU memory management and out-of-memory avoidance. Setting up RAPIDS environments (conda/containers), cloud GPU environments, and multi-GPU/cluster basics. Profiling and diagnosing performance with tools such as DLProf / Nsight. Choosing the right environment, memory strategy, or profiling step for a described performance problem.

domains.name: Visualization, Deployment, and Reproducibility
domains.notes: Communicating and operationalizing results: GPU-accelerated and standard visualization of large datasets, and integrating RAPIDS output with plotting libraries. Model deployment and monitoring at a data-science level, experiment reproducibility, versioning, and moving from notebook to a repeatable workflow. Choosing the correct visualization or deployment/reproducibility practice for a described scenario.

extra_guidance: NCA-ADS is NVIDIA's associate Accelerated Data Science certification - the GPU / RAPIDS answer to the data-science credential space, and a strong hardware-acceleration angle for the catalog (GPU architecture, GPU memory, RAPIDS, cloud GPU) rather than pure algorithms. It has PROVEN Udemy demand (existing NCA-ADS / NCP-ADS prep and practice courses are selling). CRITICAL accuracy note: NVIDIA does NOT publish official per-domain percentage weightings or the passing score for NCA-ADS, so present the domain NAMES as the exam's objective areas but mark the weights as editorial estimates (leading '~'), never as NVIDIA's official figures - state this where weights appear. Anchor EVERYTHING to the RAPIDS ecosystem and its exact vocabulary - cuDF, cudf.pandas, cuML, cuGraph, Dask / dask-cuDF, RMM memory, DLProf/Nsight - and to the recurring exam skill: choosing the RIGHT tool for a described workload (cuDF vs pandas, single-GPU vs Dask multi-GPU vs CPU, cuML vs scikit-learn, cuGraph for relationships). Practice questions MUST be predominantly scenario- and decision-based with 'BEST / FASTEST / MOST memory-efficient / MOST scalable' framing, mixed with clean concept/term-matching (which RAPIDS library, which cuML algorithm, which Dask pattern). Keep it accurate to an ASSOCIATE level: read-and-understand code and tool-selection judgment, not deep CUDA-kernel authoring. Labs are RAPIDS walkthroughs at read-and-understand depth (accelerate a pandas workflow with cudf.pandas, scale an ETL with dask-cuDF, train a cuML model, run a cuGraph algorithm, profile a pipeline). Note in the course that a professional variant (NCP-ADS) exists and this course targets the Associate. Frame the credential honestly as 'exam-focused preparation' - never promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in any form (Udemy compliance). Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a time-management strategy for the ~50-60 question, 60-minute proctored format. Do NOT invent NVIDIA's official passing score or exact fee; present the fee as approximate and advise verifying current NVIDIA pricing. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor cloud terms (AWS/Azure/GCP) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
